label: early original-phase k/t/2/o after a j/3/k/h/v/p/o/2 prefix
predicate: (t >= 1) & (t <= 3) & (phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("k"), tok("t"), tok("2"), tok("o")]) & seen([tok("j"), tok("3"), tok("k"), tok("h"), tok("v"), tok("p"), tok("o"), tok("2")])
explanation: Fires almost only on original-phase steps t=1..3 (99.4% of activations, 99.7% of mass; peaks at t=2 with 68% of mass). It never fires at t=0 and is essentially silent at t>=4, on the delimiter and in the copy phase. Within that window it depends on the current input token, strongest for k (8.6x lift) and t (7.3x), then 2 and o, weaker for p/r/j/3, and near zero for most other letters. It also depends on which tokens came earlier in the prefix: it is strongest when earlier inputs include j, 3, k, h or v. The top activations are all of the form j j [k], 3 j [t], 3 k [t]. It fires more often on the first occurrence of a token (in_first: 86% of mass). The response looks like a graded combination of current token and prefix tokens, so a boolean predicate only captures it partly: dev F1 0.55, mass recall 0.75. Many k/t at t=2 without a favorable prefix stay below threshold, and some activations come from other tokens such as p, r, j after a strong prefix.
